 Order

The petitioners vide the present petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India read with Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 seek quashing of FIR No.0693/2021 dated 03.08.2021 registered under Sections 406/498A/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 at PS.: Binda Pur, Dwarka, Delhi and all proceeding emanating therefrom in view of the Settlement Agreement dated 29.04.2023 arrived at between the parties.
W.P.(CRL) 3291/2023 page 1 of 3 This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 11/11/2023 at 03:55:17 2.
This petition is accompanied by the Settlement Agreement dated 29.04.2023 and is also supported by affidavits of all the petitioners and of respondent no.2, alongwith proofs of their respective I.Ds.
3. Petitioner nos. 1 to 6 and as also respondent no.2 are present in Court and have been identified by the Investigating Officer.
Their credentials have been verified by this Court.
4. Issue Notice.

sentences.text: Learned ASC and learned counsel for the respondent no.2 accept notice.
6. Learned ASC for the State confirms that she has no objection to the quashing of the FIR.
7. Respondent no.2 confirms that the petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2 have been granted divorce by mutual consent vide Decree of Divorce dated 04.09.2023.

She further affirms the Settlement Agreement dated 29.04.2023 whereby the petitioner no.1 has already paid her a sum of Rs.9,00,000/- and the remaining amount of Rs 2,50,000/- has been handed over to the respondent no. 2 vide DD no. 000557 issued on HDFC Bank, New Delhi, in full and final settlement of all her claims including alimony, maintenance (present, past and future), stridhan etc.
She states that she has no objection to the quashing of the present FIR.

8. In view of the settlement arrived at between the parties and following the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Jitendra Raghuvanshi & Ors. Vs. Babita Raguvanshi & Anr (2013) 4 SCC 58, Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab & Anr. (2012) 10 SCC 303 and W.P.(CRL) 3291/2023 page 2 of 3 This is a digitally signed order.

sentences.text: 9. Accordingly, the present petition is allowed and FIR No. 693/2021 dated 03.08.2021 registered under Sections 406/498A/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 at PS.: Binda Pur, Dwarka, Delhi and all proceeding emanating therefrom are quashed.

10. Needless to state that the settlement arrived at between the parties resulting in closure of all criminal proceedings inter se the parties by way of the present order will, in no way, effect the rights of the child of the petitioner no.1 and the respondent no.2 namely Bhakti vis-a-vis her parents, as may be available under law, in any manner whatsoever.
11. Accordingly, the present petition, alongwith the pending applications, if any, stands disposed of.
